units.sourceHTML: 8.4 How diff3 Merges Incomplete Lines

units.text: With ⟦0⟧, incomplete lines (see ⟦1⟧Incomplete Lines⟦2⟧) are simply copied to the output as they are found; if the merged output ends in an conflict and one of the input files ends in an incomplete line, succeeding ‘⟦3⟧’, ‘⟦4⟧’ or ‘⟦5⟧’ brackets appear somewhere other than the start of a line because they are appended to the incomplete line.
units.sourceHTML: With -m, incomplete lines (see Incomplete Lines) are simply copied to the output as they are found; if the merged output ends in an conflict and one of the input files ends in an incomplete line, succeeding ‘|||||||’, ‘=======’ or ‘>>>>>>>’ brackets appear somewhere other than the start of a line because they are appended to the incomplete line.

units.text: Without ⟦0⟧, if an ⟦1⟧ script option is specified and an incomplete line is found, ⟦2⟧ generates a warning and acts as if a newline had been present.
units.sourceHTML: Without -m, if an ed script option is specified and an incomplete line is found, diff3 generates a warning and acts as if a newline had been present.
